memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Abram set out and continued toward the Negev. Now there was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while because the famine was severe. - Gen 12:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a jarring turn. God had just promised Abram this land - and now the land is starving. A severe famine strikes the very place God led him to. Obedience did not produce comfort. Following God's call landed Abram in hardship.

We need to sit with this honestly, because it cuts against a lie we easily believe: that if we obey God, life will go smoothly. Abram did exactly what God said, went exactly where God led - and found famine. Being in the centre of God's will does not guarantee an easy road. Sometimes it leads straight into difficulty.

Notice too what Abram does: "went down to Egypt." Egypt, throughout Scripture, often represents the world's resources - the place people turn when they stop trusting God's provision. Abram doesn't pray here. He doesn't build an altar. He acts on his own instincts, and, as we'll see, it goes badly.

The pressure of hardship reveals what we truly trust. When the famine hits, do we turn to God or to our own solutions? Jesus faced His own wilderness hunger and answered, "Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God" (Matt 4:4). Hardship in God's will is not evidence He has failed you. Hold on. Don't run to Egypt.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you assume obedience should make life easier?
- Where are you tempted to run to your own "Egypt" instead of trusting God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, when following You leads into hardship, keep me from running to my own solutions. Help me trust Your provision in the famine rather than trusting my own way out.
Amen.
